stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung completes India and Vietnam state visits with major trade and energy deals
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung conducted a week-long diplomatic swing to India (April 20-21) and Vietnam (April 21-24), signing frameworks to nearly double South Korea-India trade to $50 billion by 2030 and concluding 73 business deals and 12 inter-governmental agreements in Hanoi, including nuclear energy and supply chain cooperation. Vietnam's leader To Lam pledged support for resuming inter-Korean dialogue, and Korean financial institutions including Korea Eximbank, KEPCO, and IBK signed financing and licensing agreements for Vietnam's nuclear power program. Lee's approval rating climbed to 67 percent on the back of the diplomatic results.

stories.headline: New Bank of Korea governor Shin Hyun-song takes office, signals CBDC priority and cautious monetary policy
stories.summary: Shin Hyun-song was inaugurated as Bank of Korea governor on April 21, succeeding Rhee Chang-yong after a four-year term. In his inaugural address and first public statements, Shin prioritized central bank digital currencies and bank-issued deposit tokens over stablecoins, pledged cautious and flexible monetary policy amid Middle East oil shock risks, and outlined plans to internationalize the won through 24-hour FX trading. Shin also met Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol to coordinate fiscal-monetary policy. Analysts note Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% has raised the possibility of an unexpected BOK rate hike at the May 28 meeting.

stories.headline: Prosecutors seek 30-year additional prison term for Yoon Suk-yeol over 2024 Pyongyang drone flights
stories.summary: South Korean special prosecutors on April 24 requested a further 30-year prison sentence for impeached former President Yoon Suk-yeol, alleging he ordered military drone flights over Pyongyang in October 2024 to provoke a North Korean response and thereby justify his subsequent declaration of martial law. Yoon, already serving a life sentence for insurrection, delivered a final statement in the case on April 25; his defense team expressed confidence of acquittal.

stories.headline: Samsung chip workers threaten 18-day strike over $400K bonus demands as production drops
stories.summary: More than 40,000 Samsung Electronics unionized workers rallied at the Pyeongtaek chip facility this week demanding performance bonuses comparable to rival SK Hynix, with some estimates citing $400,000 per worker; the union set a May 21 strike date. A walkout has already begun reducing chip output. The Labor Minister described Samsung as a 'people's company' and acknowledged workers' demands had merit. Analysts warn a prolonged strike could cost Samsung up to 30 trillion won and deepen a global DRAM shortage.

stories.headline: People Power Party struggles to field June 3 local election candidates as polls show record-low support
stories.summary: South Korea's main opposition People Power Party (PPP) confirmed Rep. Choo Kyung-ho as its Daegu mayoral candidate and finalized nominations in other races ahead of the June 3 local and by-elections, but has struggled to recruit contenders across the country, falling back on veteran politicians. A survey this week showed PPP support at a record low of 15 percent versus the ruling Democratic Party's plurality. Separate controversy arose over the semiconductor cluster relocation debate, where local election candidates clashed over the Yongin chip project's location.

stories.headline: South Korea Q1 GDP surges 1.7% on AI-driven chip exports, KOSPI crosses 6,500
stories.summary: South Korea's economy grew 1.7% quarter-on-quarter in Q1 2026, its fastest pace in nearly six years, driven almost entirely by semiconductor exports benefiting from global AI investment demand. The benchmark KOSPI index briefly crossed the 6,500 mark intraday for the first time. Analysts at ING raised their 2026 GDP forecast to 2.8%, while warning that energy disruptions from the Middle East conflict could slow growth in Q2 and push inflation higher.

stories.headline: US partially restricts intelligence sharing with South Korea after minister publicly identifies suspected North Korean nuclear site
stories.summary: Washington partially restricted satellite intelligence sharing with Seoul after South Korea's minister for inter-Korean affairs, Chung, publicly referenced a suspected nuclear facility at Kusong during a policy briefing. President Lee described allegations of a classified intelligence leak as 'absurd,' arguing the site was already publicly documented. The PPP convened unilateral parliamentary sessions to press the government on the incident, and later declared the South Korea-US alliance in 'total crisis.'

stories.headline: ROK Air Force formally acknowledges 2021 F-15K mid-air collision caused by pilots taking selfies
stories.summary: South Korea's Board of Audit and Inspection found that a 2021 mid-air collision between two ROK Air Force F-15K fighter jets was caused by a wingman pilot taking commemorative photos and videos during the flight, including a selfie to mark his final mission with the unit. The air force apologized publicly; one pilot was fined and ordered to repay a portion of the approximately $600,000 in repair costs. The wingman pilot has since left the military for commercial aviation.

stories.headline: US-ROK military exercises and joint training continue amid alliance activities
stories.summary: US and South Korean forces conducted multiple joint training events this week, including exercise Freedom Flag 26-1 at an ROK air base, where USAF, ROKAF, and US Marine Corps personnel reaffirmed interoperability. Separately, a US-ROK civil-military crisis response workshop at Camp Humphreys focused on humanitarian assistance and disaster preparedness coordination across USFK, CFC, and inter-agency partners.

stories.headline: Hanwha Defense USA secures US Department of War contract for medium unmanned surface vessels
stories.summary: Hanwha Defense USA and Miami-based Magnet Defense announced a strategic partnership to produce medium unmanned surface vessels (MUSVs) for the US Department of War, marking a further expansion of South Korea's Hanwha Group into the US defense market. Forbes covered the broader strategic rationale of Hanwha reinforcing America's defense industrial base, citing a $1.3 billion manufacturing facility at Pine Bluff Arsenal in Arkansas.

stories.headline: South Korea's big four banks post record Q1 profits but NPL coverage ratios decline sharply
stories.summary: Korea's four largest financial groups—KB, Shinhan, Hana, and Woori—reported a combined 5.32 trillion won in net profit for Q1 2026, a record, driven by higher lending rates and the stock market rally. However, a separate report found their average non-performing loan coverage ratio dropped 18.2 percentage points to 153.8% as corporate distress from delayed economic recovery spreads into the financial sector.

stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung attacks award-winning Daejang-dong newspaper report as fabrication, demands retraction
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung publicly criticized a national newspaper that received a journalism award for a report on the Daejang-dong real estate development scandal, calling it a 'tremendous fabrication' and calling for the award to be returned. Lee alleged the report erroneously identified him as a recorded voice, which he said cost the Democratic Party the previous presidential election.

stories.headline: Editorial pressure mounts on DPK and PPP to nominate presidential anti-corruption inspector
stories.summary: The Korea Times editorial board and Yonhap's editorial roundup both called on the ruling Democratic Party and opposition PPP to end their deadlock over nominating a special inspector general for investigating presidential family and aide corruption. President Lee has requested nominations since the start of his administration; both parties have failed to act, blaming each other for the delay.
